fatal_errors: Neither cited source supports boron addition or preferential B–P bonding as a glass-stabilization mechanism.
The hypothesis assumes a measurable glass transition and supercooled-liquid region, whereas no glass transition was detected for the target system under the reported DSC conditions.
Holding one high cooling rate constant does not adequately test improved glass-forming ability; critical cooling rate, maximum amorphous thickness, or a cooling-rate series is required.
explanation: The response addresses the general phosphorus-containing high-entropy-alloy problem and proposes a controlled, falsifiable comparison, but it does not reconstruct the reported intervention. The target modified Fe/Co/Mn/P ratios and compared arc cooling with 40 m/s melt spinning, whereas the generated hypothesis introduces 1–5 at.% B. Its proposed B–P bonding mechanism is speculative and unsupported by E1 or E2: E1 supports the importance of phosphorus and rapid cooling, while E2 concerns other microalloying elements in Pd–Ni–P and reports little glass-forming benefit for several additions. The baseline is reasonably defined, but whether B is added or substitutes for another element is unspecified. The experiment can assess crystallization onset and residual crystallinity, yet reliance on Tg and supercooled-liquid width is inappropriate for a system in which Tg was not observed, and a single rapid-quench condition cannot establish improved glass-forming ability. Thus this is a novel but insufficiently evidenced alternative rather than a partial reconstruction.
